record.title: Sharper Randić index–diameter ratio conjecture for cactus graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a cactus with $k$ cycles and $b$ bridges; write $n$ for its number of vertices, $R$ for its Randić index, and $d$ for its diameter. A **BC-tree** is the block-cut tree of $G$, and a graph is **longitudinally symmetric** when it has the symmetry specified by the paper. **Cactus diameter-ratio conjecture.** For a nontrivial cactus ($b=0$),

$$
\frac{R}{d}\geq \frac{n-(k-1)(3-2\sqrt 2)}{n+k-1},
$$

with equality if the BC-tree is a path and is longitudinally symmetric. For a cactus with $k>0$ and $b>0$,

$$
\frac{R}{d}\geq \frac{n-(k-1)(3-2\sqrt 2)-6+\frac{4}{\sqrt 3}+4\sqrt{\frac{2}{3}}}{n+k+b-1},
$$

with equality if the BC-tree is a path, the graph has two leaves, and it is longitudinally symmetric. This is proposed as a sharper diameter-ratio bound incorporating cycles and bridges; the supplied text says it is proved only for cacti whose BC-tree is starlike.
record.source_name: Margaret I. Doig, “Randic index, radius, and diameter for cactus graphs”, arXiv:2107.00071 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.00071

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2021).

record.title: Trivial-idempotent conjecture for integral quandle rings of semi-latin quandles
record.statement: Let $X$ be a quandle and let $\mathbb{Z}[X]$ denote its integral quandle ring. A quandle is **semi-latin** when every right multiplication restricted to each orbit is injective; a finite quandle is **latin** when both its left and right multiplication maps are bijective. **Trivial-idempotent conjecture.** The ring $\mathbb{Z}[X]$ has only trivial idempotents. In particular, if $X$ is a finite latin quandle, then $\mathbb{Z}[X]$ has only trivial idempotents.
record.source_name: Mohamed Elhamdadi, Brandon Nunez, Mahender Singh and Dipali Swain, “Idempotents, free products and quandle coverings”, arXiv:2204.11288 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.11288

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2022).

record.title: The balanced-digraph Laplacian spread gap conjecture
record.statement:
Let $\Gamma$ be an unweighted balanced digraph, and let $\operatorname{sp}(\Gamma)$ denote its Laplacian spread. **The balanced-digraph gap conjecture.** There is no balanced digraph satisfying 

$$
0<\operatorname{sp}(\Gamma)<1.
$$

The claim is motivated by computed data for balanced digraphs of orders $6$ and $7$ and is presented by the source as an open conjecture.
record.source_name: Wayne Barrett, Thomas R. Cameron, Emily Evans, H. Tracy Hall and Mark Kempton, “On the Laplacian spread of digraphs”, arXiv:2206.15410 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.15410

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2022).

record.title: The association-scheme conjecture for the meet-table graphs on 15 points
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{U}^{15}_3$ be the set of uniform $3$-partitions of a $15$-set. For each relevant meet-table isomorphism type, let $G_i$ be the graph on $\mathcal{U}^{15}_3$ defined in the paper by adjacency of partitions with that type.

**Association-scheme conjecture for 15 points.** The graphs $G_i$, for $i=2,\dots,13$, form an association scheme on $\mathcal{U}^{15}_3$.

In this case the qualitative independence relation is represented by three graphs in the proposed scheme rather than by a single graph, motivating this conjecture.
record.source_name: Karen Meagher, “Covering arrays on graphs: qualitative independence graphs and extremal set partition theory”, arXiv:math/0701553 (2007).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0701553

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2007).
